To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of SUDS can reduce urban surface flood water risks, but the effectiveness of their performance in extreme flood events is not well known.

the use of SUDS in the urban drainage network can significantly reduce the flood risk in the urban area, and that a GIS-based integrated 1D and 2D model is an effective tool to demonstrate the effectiveness of SUDS.

(i) the use of SUDS can reduce urban surface flood risks and pollution impact on the receiving waters; (ii) the SUDS can be strategically located to maximize flood and pollution reduction benefits; (iii) SUDS performance effectiveness may be quantified by the use of coupled 1D and 2D models; (iv) SUDSLOC is a useful tool for the selection, location and quantification of the performance of SUDS controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and demonstration of a novel and innovative modelling approach to assist in the management of surface water flood risks in urban environments.

the use of SUDS to improve resilience to extreme events in urban areas and the role of SUDSLOC as an integrated tool to assist with the selection of SUDS options and their location within the urban drainage network.
the development of a robust approach to the management of urban surface flooding risks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SUDS are not a panacea for the problems of surface water management in cities, and that the use of SUDS is a complex and multi-faceted issue.

the integrated modelling approach and SUDS selection tool can be used as a robust decision support tool for urban drainage infrastructure management and the selection and location of SUDS to manage surface water flood risk.
the use of GIS and SUDS in the management of surface water flood risk is a very promising approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a SUDSLOC model has been developed to support the decision-making process for the strategic selection and placement of SUDS controls.
the SUDS approach to urban drainage is a valuable tool for managing surface water flooding risks and the resilience of the drainage infrastructure.
the SUDS performance can be quantified in terms of flood reduction and the SUDS design criteria can be derived from the SUDS selection process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrated modelling approach can help to identify the best SUDS solutions in terms of flood reduction and water quality improvement.
the use of SUDS in urban drainage systems can reduce urban surface flood risk and improve the resilience of urban drainage systems to extreme events.
the SUDS selection tool is a powerful tool to support decision making and to communicate the benefits of SUDS in flood risk management.
